sections.title: Hook & Intuition (1 min)
lecture_lines: Can four points always form a square?
A circle makes this easy to see.
But what about a random squiggle?
The Toeplitz conjecture asks this question.
[Asset: SquareConstruction] The answer is always yes.
animations: Draw a set of four random points #FFFFFF on screen.
Appear a faint circle passing through them in #00FFFF.
Animate a chaotic spline connecting the points in #FFFF00.
Transform the points to form a square in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Configuration Space (1 min)
lecture_lines: We map point pairs to a surface.
Points close together sit near the diagonal.
This configuration space visualizes every possible pair.
animations: Create a 2D plane grid #FFFFFF labeled with coordinates.
Animate two points moving on the plane in #00FFFF.
Show their midpoint as a target indicator in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Topological Mapping (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: We define midpoint and distance functions.
We seek where these functions vanish.
[Asset: TopologyMapping] These functions must hit zero.
animations: Define f(x) as midpoint function in #FFFFFF on screen.
Graph f(x) and f(-x) on the same plane in #00FFFF.
Show where the two paths intersect.
Add a terminal green anchor icon at the intersection point.
Fade the intersection point to indicate the solved square.

sections.title: The Symmetry Argument (1 min)
lecture_lines: [Asset: SymmetryArgument] The zero point is inevitable.
animations: Show a coordinate system with rotation in #FFFFFF.
Flash a green target icon to prove the zero exists.

sections.title: Conclusion & Open Frontiers (0.5 min)
lecture_lines: For smooth curves, it is proven.
General cases remain an open challenge.
animations: Place equation 'f(x) = 0' in row D using #FFFFFF.
Arrange icons for 'square' and 'curve' in row B, C in #FFFF00.
Flash icon to finalize the summary.
